persona_review.selected_persona: Name & Archetype: Milo, age 10, a curious builder and picky first-time code explorer. Persona specified by the user. Environment & Constraints: Small laptop and 390px phone; keyboard navigation; reduced-motion preference; slow or unavailable optional effects. Picky Obsessions: Unexplained code words, tiny controls, dull styling, lost instructions, and motion that obscures meaning. Tool Attack Plan: jg and direct source inspection; Playwright screenshots, interaction and boundary probes; axe WCAG A/AA checks; npm tests, build, smoke and audit; GitHub awesome-list research; Jev brainstorming, bounded decision and final gate.

iteration.adversarial_review: - [ISS-1.01] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/codebase-bead-maze.html, lede and hints] Tool Evidence: Baseline Playwright screenshot .scratch/review/before-desktop.png and full HTML read show dense reference terminology with no separate visual key for beads, tracks, and arrows. Critique: I want to know what each part means before I click. Acceptance Criterion: Three visible, plain-language explanations connect each visual to a code concept. - [ISS-1.02] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/codebase-bead-maze.html, header and styles] Tool Evidence: Baseline screenshot shows beige surfaces, a Georgia title, and uniform low-emphasis panels. Critique: This feels like a document, not a cool toy to explore. Acceptance Criterion: A coherent playful color palette, expressive type, bead artwork, and distinct discovery tools. - [ISS-1.03] [Severity: HIGH] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js, showGraph and selectFile] Tool Evidence: Full module read shows no guided first interaction; only selecting a file changes the inspector. Critique: What should I do first, and what did that arrow just do? Acceptance Criterion: A three-step guide follows a real graph edge and explains source and target perspectives. - [ISS-1.04] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/codebase-bead-maze.html, scene-controls and file-list styles] Tool Evidence: Baseline CSS uses 5px vertical control padding with 12px type and 7px vertical file-button padding. Critique: My finger needs a bigger target. Acceptance Criterion: Primary buttons, scene controls and file choices offer at least 44px height. - [ISS-1.05] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js, renderFiles] Tool Evidence: Source returns an empty list and count only when no file matches. Critique: Did I break the toy? How do I get my beads back? Acceptance Criterion: No-match message, recovery advice, and Clear search action restore all files and search focus. - [ISS-1.06] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/bead-scene.js, makeReferences and select] Tool Evidence: Source draws static reference lines and immediately changes bead scale; there is no meaningful animated feedback or motion control. Critique: Let me see which way the connection goes, with some satisfying motion! Acceptance Criterion: Modern locally shipped libraries animate discovery, selection and source-to-target reference travel, with reduced-motion and explicit off support. - [ISS-1.07] [Severity: LOW] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js, selectFile and showGraph] Tool Evidence: Baseline zero-reference inspector renders only References (0) and Referenced by (0); empty maps keep a selection prompt. Critique: Is a bead with no arrows broken? Acceptance Criterion: Isolated beads, empty maps and no-reference guides receive truthful explanations and usable controls.
iteration.fixes: - [FIX-1.01 -> ISS-1.01] docs/codebase-bead-maze.html and docs/playground.css: Added bead/file, track/folder and arrow/uses explanation cards plus a directional color key. Verified by desktop/mobile screenshots and browser accessibility checks. - [FIX-1.02 -> ISS-1.02] docs/codebase-bead-maze.html and docs/playground.css: Rebuilt the page in lavender, lime and coral with responsive cards, native SVG bead artwork and a distinct guide. Verified at 320, 390, 768, 980 and 1440px without horizontal overflow. - [FIX-1.03 -> ISS-1.03] docs/discovery-guide.js and docs/codebase-map.js: Added deterministic three-step discovery using actual graph source/target IDs, manual-selection reset, completion and replay. Keyboard and real-reference browser probes pass. - [FIX-1.04 -> ISS-1.04] docs/playground.css: Increased actionable control heights to 44px or more; added focus styles and a skip link. Keyboard probes and axe checks pass. - [FIX-1.05 -> ISS-1.05] docs/codebase-map.js and HTML: Added visible empty-search recovery, including Unicode and markup-shaped search coverage. Clear search restores three fixture files and focuses the input. - [FIX-1.06 -> ISS-1.06] docs/playground-motion.js, docs/bead-scene.js and docs/vendor/: Pinned Anime.js 4.5.0 and canvas-confetti 1.9.4, preserving licenses. Added staggered entrances, spring bead pops, halo feedback, finite directional lights and completion confetti. Saved preference and live OS reduced-motion changes stop effects. Vendored files match installed distribution files via cmp; static smoke passes. - [FIX-1.07 -> ISS-1.07] docs/codebase-map.js and docs/discovery-guide.js: Added solo-bead, empty-project, self-reference and disconnected-map explanations. Browser boundary probes pass. Baseline and first implementation verification: 12/12 unit tests, build, existing WebGL/mobile/static-export browser smoke and syntax checks passed.

iteration.adversarial_review: - [ISS-2.01] [Severity: HIGH] [Location: docs/discovery-guide.js and mobile layout] Tool Evidence: .scratch/review/after-mobile.png shows the guide below the full maze; activating it leaves the bead and its narration separated by scrolling. Critique: I cannot watch the bead while reading what happened. Acceptance Criterion: Active mobile instructions and a visible next action sit beside the maze; keyboard focus follows that action. - [ISS-2.02] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js, showGraph fallback instructions] Tool Evidence: Forced missing Three.js route produces canvas2d while the original hint still promises drag orbit and keyboard camera controls. Critique: I followed the directions and the toy would not spin. Acceptance Criterion: Flat view explains its actual controls and hides unsupported camera actions. - [ISS-2.03] [Severity: HIGH] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js selectFile; docs/discovery-guide.js render] Tool Evidence: npm run test:ui reported color-contrast violations on guide-step, guide-body, detail-body and connection-note while opacity transitions ran. Critique: The explanation should stay readable when it changes. Acceptance Criterion: Updated text remains fully opaque while animated; axe passes immediately after interaction. - [ISS-2.04] [Severity: MEDIUM] [Location: docs/bead-scene.js, makeReferences; docs/playground-motion.js, animate] Tool Evidence: Source inspection found particles created when user motion was enabled even if the optional Anime.js import returned null; animate then returned no handle. Critique: A frozen dot is confusing, not an animation. Acceptance Criterion: Missing effects leave core interaction intact, no traveling particles and referenceMotion idle. - [ISS-2.05] [Severity: LOW] [Location: docs/discovery-guide.js, End tour] Tool Evidence: Source inspection shows end-tour focus targeting canvas; the flat fallback canvas has no tabIndex and cannot receive that focus. Critique: Do not lose my place when I end the tour. Acceptance Criterion: End tour focuses the WebGL canvas or the fallback file-search control, both tested. - [ISS-2.06] [Severity: NITPICK] [Location: docs/codebase-map.js, warning-count] Tool Evidence: Desktop screenshot displayed About this map (1 notes). Critique: It should say one note. Acceptance Criterion: Singular and plural note labels agree with the count.

iteration.adversarial_review: - [ISS-3.01] [Severity: HIGH] [Location: docs/playground-motion.js, revealPlayground] Tool Evidence: A fresh fallback-page accessibility run caught color-contrast failures on lede and explanation-card text during their entrance fade. Critique: The first instructions must be readable as soon as they appear. Acceptance Criterion: Entrances keep text fully opaque, including during initial loading; immediate axe checks pass. - [ISS-3.02] [Severity: LOW] [Location: package.json, @axe-core/playwright development dependency] Tool Evidence: npm package metadata for the initially chosen 4.14.0 requires Node >=22.12.0, beyond the project's documented >=22 support. Registry metadata for 4.13.0 has no added Node engine constraint. Critique: The UI checks should work with the project's stated setup. Acceptance Criterion: Keep a compatible pinned accessibility tool and rerun all checks.
iteration.fixes: - [FIX-3.01 -> ISS-3.01] docs/playground-motion.js and scripts/ui-review.mjs: Removed entrance opacity animation, kept staggered movement, and removed the initial accessibility-test delay so checks include entrances. Fresh desktop and fallback accessibility checks pass. - [FIX-3.02 -> ISS-3.02] package.json and package-lock.json: Pinned @axe-core/playwright 4.13.0, then reran the UI suite, unit tests, build, smoke and dependency audit.

iteration.adversarial_review: - [ISS-4.01] [Severity: LOW] [Location: docs/bead-scene.js, layoutLabels] Tool Evidence: Independent Playwright stress probe selected 30 files, disabled file names, and reset the camera. It found 18 elements matching .file-label.is-selected instead of one. Source inspection showed class updates occurred after early exits for hidden labels. Critique: A label should only carry a selection marker for the current bead, even while hidden. Acceptance Criterion: After 30 selections in a crowded 80-file map, hiding labels and resetting leaves exactly one selected label, visible and matching the current file.
iteration.fixes: - [FIX-4.01 -> ISS-4.01] docs/bead-scene.js and scripts/ui-review.mjs: Synchronize selection and hover classes before any label-visibility early exit. Added a crowded 80-file browser regression with 30 selections, hidden file names and camera reset. The current selected label remains the only selected label.

iteration.adversarial_review:
Final clean review of the exercised UI scope: zero remaining persona complaints. Tool checks: node --check for changed application/test modules; npm run build; npm test (12 passed, 0 failed); npm run smoke (WebGL, hover/picking, search, rescan, errors, retina canvas, mobile fallback and static export); npm run test:ui (keyboard guide, real reference direction, interrupted tours, empty-search recovery, 320–1440px reflow, mobile narration/focus, live reduced motion, stored preference, empty/isolated/self-reference maps, fallback, unavailable effects/storage, crowded-map label-state regression, and zero WCAG A/AA axe violations in four states); npm audit --audit-level=low (0 vulnerabilities); git diff --check; cmp against both pinned npm effect distributions. Manual rendered inspection: .scratch/verification/playground-desktop.png and playground-mobile-tour.png; real-project browser probe reported no uncaught errors, no HTTP failures and no viewport overflow. Jev use: brainstorm Nouls supported a real-edge tour (0.89), directional lights (0.86) and larger controls with recovery guidance (0.88). Ambient-particle competition was uncertain (0.78); the implementation uses finite contextual effects. Bounded library decision selected Anime.js plus canvas-confetti (0.99), with no contradicted requirements. UI control flow and tour state remain deterministic local code; no model integration was added to the product. Limits: These are empirical checks of the local Chrome build and the states listed above, not a claim about every browser or every possible repository.
Independent reasoning review after Jev escalation: the first Jev gate verified all three completion claims (confidence 1.00, 0.98, 0.98) but escalated patch uncertainty (safe_to_apply 0.66; composite 0.758; low-confidence blast-radius/test-gap rubric judgments). That was not automatic acceptance. Host source review confirmed no changes to the scanner, server, layout algorithm or build script. Runtime stress checks confirmed visibly advancing effects, a settled idle canvas, cancellation under motion-off, and no uncaught errors; the hidden-label defect found in that review was fixed in iteration 4. The source and runtime review informed the decision to proceed within the already authorized UI scope.
The final incremental Jev gate verified the updated tests and crowded-map regression (confidence 1.00, 0.98, 0.88), while again escalating patch uncertainty (safe_to_apply 0.74; composite 0.837; blast-radius confidence 0.00). The host reasoning review checked the exact invariant: each label now receives is-selected iff its unique file ID equals the selected ID before any continue, so hiding a label cannot preserve a stale marker. The change affects only label classes; validation still enforces unique node IDs. The crowded-map test and the independent real-project stress probe validate that invariant in the rendered UI. Neither Jev gate was treated as automatic patch approval.
iteration.fixes: None required - all verification checks passed.
